title: CISA KEV adds Cisco BroadWorks XXE & Openwave Webtop
sum: CISA added two new known-exploited entries: Cisco BroadWorks XXE (actively exploited) and an Openwave Webtop resource-transfer flaw, with an immediate federal patching deadline.

title: Microsoft Outlook zero-day steals NTLMv2 hashes
sum: Actively exploited Outlook zero-day delivers crafted email files to steal NTLMv2 hashes. Patch per CVE-2026-124194 before the Nov 24 deadline.

title: SitusAMC breach exposes major US bank data
sum: Attackers breached fintech SitusAMC on Nov 12, stealing corporate, accounting and legal records. JPMorgan, Citi and Morgan Stanley assess customer exposure; no encryption used.

title: Radware breach leaks customer cloud access keys
sum: Attackers hit an unauthenticated Cloud WAF management API on Nov 19, exfiltrating customer details and cloud access keys from 12,500+ enterprise carriers. Radware rotated credentials.
ctl: M1026 Privileged Account Management — rotate keys

title: Check Point management servers breached in 22 orgs
sum: GreyNoise-tracked campaign GT13 exploits multiple vulns to compromise Check Point security management servers across 22 orgs, holding persistent access since Oct 17.

title: GL.iNet cloud flaw exploited to infect routers
sum: Actively exploited GL.iNet cloud remote-management flaw lets attackers drop custom malware, backdoors and reverse shells on routers and KVM devices.
ctl: M1042 Disable or Remove Feature or Program — disable cloud mgmt

title: Cleverbridge breach steals card numbers & CVVs
sum: E-commerce platform Cleverbridge confirmed payment card numbers and CVVs were stolen, with broad impact possible across its SaaS/software client base.

title: EU Academy data theft confirmed
sum: Attackers used the ARTeX pen-testing framework to breach the EU Academy learning hub, stealing personal data and disrupting the Sysper HR platform.
ctl: M1027 Password Policies — review credential reuse

title: McDonald's Japan customer database breach
sum: Customer database accessed exposing purchase history, IP addresses and location data; no names, emails or payment info taken.

title: ShinyHunters resurfaces with historic PGP keys
sum: ShinyHunters posted on a new Tor leak site signed with 2020-era PGP keys, suggesting the real group's infrastructure survived the FBI arrests. Watch for new leaks.
